text.p: Here are highlights of stories in Romania's press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
Business:
ADEVARUL
- The leu has bobbed up against the dollar at currency exchange shops to reach 5,800-6,000, up from last week's 6,400.
- The Senate's economic commission finalised an amendment to the land restitution law allowing foreign investors to own land if their company is registered in Romania.
- Liberal senators discussed amendment to cut profit tax to 30 percent from 38 percent previously.

- Bankcoop SA private bank is confronted with a wave of withdrawals in branches across the country after a recent row between the bank president and its main shareholder. The bank says it has enough liquidity to honour withdrawals.
- Raising energy prices will aim to equilibrate the balance in the Romanian economy, with more money now than goods and services on the market, the newspaper says.
CAPITAL
- Romania will bring electricity prices in line with world prices of $50 per megawatt.
- Romanians will have to pay 220 lei (4 cents) for a kilowatt, up from a previous 73 lei (1 cent).
ROMANIA LIBERA
- Former Polish President Lech Walesa advised Romanian President Emil Constantinescu to start reform by privatising industrial giants.
- Government postponed issuing social protection and economic reform measures until new loan accords are agreed with the World Bank and the IMF.
- Prime Minister Victor Ciorbea said social protection measures due in three weeks time will apply for January, too.
EVENIMENTUL ZILEI
- Romanian state-owned Tarom airline is negotiating with Boeing to buy eight aircraft over the next four years as part of plans to restructure the company.
ZIUA
- Tourism Minister Akos Birtalan said he wanted the same hotel fares for Romanians and foreigners. He said students, pensioners, unemployed and journalists will get discounts.
CURIERUL NATIONAL
- A group of U.S. investors led by investment holding CMG Communications is looking at investing some $10 billion in Romania in privatised industry, stock exchange and market research projects.
General:
ROMANIA LIBERA
- Romania and Poland will support each other's bid for early NATO admission, Constantinescu and counterpart Aleksander Kwasniewski said during Romanian president's visit to Warsaw.
- Coal miners' leader Miron Cosma raised a monthly 135 million lei from members of the Jiu Valley labour unions.
- Some 200 miners in the coal town of Petrosani staged protest askingthat their leader, Cosma, be freed from detention pending a probe on suspicions of undermining state authority.
EVENIMENTUL ZILEI
- Telephone threats to kidnap President Emil Constantinescu's mother and sister proved to be a hoax.
ADEVARUL

- Liberal leader and lawyer Niculae Cerveni dropped case of bank founder carged with fraud after pressure from centrist ruling coalition leaders who said his position clashed with the coalition's anti-corruption campaign.
- Leftist Party of Social Democracy of ex-President Ion Iliescu to start national conference on Friday to reshape party and elect new leadership after losing elections last November.
LIBERTATEA
- Ciorbea says he fulfilled most of electoral promisses made before being elected Bucharest mayor. ($=4,771 lei) -- Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
